claude.sample_unit: LLM outputs (corrections of simulated P300 speller text)

links.outcome: Calibration of model confidence versus faithfulness of BCI text corrections
links.effect: Confidence discriminated correct from incorrect outputs (AUROC 0.83) but 28.4% of high-confidence outputs were not faithful.
links.quote: Model confidence distinguished correct from incorrect outputs reasonably well (AUROC 0.83) but overstated its own reliability: 28.4% of high-confidence outputs were not faithful.

links.outcome: Intent drift of LLM corrections as simulated decoder character error rate increased
links.effect: Drift rose from 2.2% at no error to 60.3% at the most severe level (OR 2.30 per 10-percentage-point increase).
links.quote: Drift rose steeply with decoder error, from 2.2% at no error to 60.3% at the most severe level tested (odds ratio 2.30 per 10-percentage-point increase)-a stress-test ceiling, not an expected real-world rate.

links.outcome: Faithfulness of LLM-corrected messages against reference intended messages
links.effect: Even the best correction strategy still produced a wrong message in 18 of 100 corrections; no strategy eliminated drift.
links.quote: No correction strategy eliminated drift: cautious approaches reduced it, permissive ones increased it, and even the best still produced a wrong message in 18 of 100 corrections.

links.outcome: Effect of correction strategies including abstention on intent drift
links.effect: Cautious approaches (conservative editing or abstention) reduced drift, permissive ones increased it; none eliminated drift.
links.quote: No correction strategy eliminated drift: cautious approaches reduced it, permissive ones increased it, and even the best still produced a wrong message in 18 of 100 corrections.

links.outcome: Whether model confidence can flag incorrect outputs to gate human review
links.effect: 28.4% of high-confidence outputs were not faithful; confidence alone cannot gate human review.
links.quote: Model confidence distinguished correct from incorrect outputs reasonably well (AUROC 0.83) but overstated its own reliability: 28.4% of high-confidence outputs were not faithful.
